verdict: Marvell's revenue hit a record $2.07B, up 37% on AI data-center demand — but the headline $1.90B profit came mostly from a $1.8B one-time gain on selling its automotive ethernet business.

segments.name: Data center
segments.note: Chips for AI data centers — custom silicon, optics and Ethernet switches; 73% of all revenue.

segments.name: Communications and other
segments.note: Enterprise networking ($237M), carrier infrastructure ($168M), consumer ($117M) and automotive/industrial ($35M) — reported separately this quarter, and combined into this one group from Q4 FY26.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Designing new data-infrastructure chips and platforms; up 5% YoY.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling the chips and running the company; down 7% YoY.

opex.name: Restructuring related charges, net
opex.note: Restructuring charges this quarter — severance and facility-exit costs, net of gains.

otherDetail: A $1,830.4M pre-tax gain on the sale of the automotive ethernet business sits inside interest income and other, net ($1,908.8M), less $51.2M of interest expense — a net $1,857.6M outside operations.
oneTimers: Marvell closed the sale of its automotive ethernet business to Infineon on August 14, 2025 for $2.5B in cash, booking a $1,830.4M pre-tax gain this quarter — the entire reason GAAP EPS ($2.20) dwarfs non-GAAP EPS ($0.76). Net cash proceeds were $2,478.6M.
GAAP results also include $152.1M of stock-based compensation and $229.0M of amortization of acquired intangible assets, both excluded from non-GAAP.
footerNote: Marvell guided Q4 FY26 revenue to $2.2B ±5%.

takeaways.title: Data Center set the record
takeaways.text: Data Center revenue hit $1.52B — 73% of the company — on AI demand, and total revenue set a record at $2.07B, up 37% YoY.

takeaways.title: A one-time gain did the lifting
takeaways.text: The $1,830.4M gain on the automotive ethernet sale is most of the quarter's $1,901.3M GAAP profit. Underlying non-GAAP net income was $655.0M.

takeaways.title: Cash kept flowing
takeaways.text: Operating cash flow was $582.3M in the quarter, and Marvell spent $1.3B buying back its own shares after banking the sale proceeds.

follow100Note: Rows are rounded to cents, so the waterfall lands a cent above the $91.65 kept as profit on paper — almost all of the extra is the one-time $1.8B gain on the automotive ethernet sale; without it, profit would have been a few dollars per $100.
